analysis.objective: Finish the Check system and extend the demo from 'Sync loads' to 'Sync + Transform with safe failure'. That means: Breaking Change detection against a per-Environment schema snapshot, user-declared per-table Checks in Pipeline YAML (not_null, accepted_values, min_rows, freshness), a dbt Transform Step run through dbtRunner with dbt tests reported as Checks, dedicated sanitized errors for an unreachable Source, an unreachable Warehouse and an empty Source table, and the same demo Pipelines running unchanged on a DuckDB Warehouse. All of it is proven in the Docker E2E job under the 100% coverage gate.
analysis.successDefinition: Done when ALL hold. (1) After every successful Sync table, the snapshot table `_adops_schema_snapshots` in each Warehouse records that table's column names and types. A later run that finds a renamed, dropped or retyped column in a Source table raises a sanitized Breaking Change error. That Sync Step fails, and every Step after it in YAML order is not run. Added columns are not a Breaking Change, and the first run with no snapshot records a baseline instead of failing. (2) `adops accept-schema <pipeline> <table>` records the current Source shape as the new snapshot for the chosen Environment, and the next run passes. (3) Pipeline YAML accepts per-table user-declared Checks: not_null, accepted_values, min_rows and freshness. The loader validates them, `adops validate` rejects malformed ones with a clear error, and pure domain rules decide each verdict from facts the adapters measured. freshness takes its 'now' from an injected clock, so the same facts always give the same verdict. A failed Check fails its Step and stops later Steps, and skip_checks with a reason still applies (ADR-0013). (4) A Transform Step in Pipeline YAML runs the demo's dbt project (models plus dbt tests over the dlt raw_<source> schema) through dbtRunner behind a new Transform port, with no dagster-dbt. adops reads run_results.json. Each dbt test becomes a Check whose verdict a domain rule decides from the measured failure count. A failed dbt test fails the Transform Step. (5) An unreachable Source, an unreachable Warehouse and an empty Source table each produce a dedicated, sanitized error that names the Pipeline, Step and table and never shows a secret value. Tests assert this. (6) The demo scaffold from `adops init --demo` contains the dbt project, and its dbt profile settings use Secret References, not values. The same demo Pipelines run unchanged against a DuckDB Warehouse (dlt duckdb destination plus dbt-duckdb) as well as Postgres. (7) uv.lock resolves with dbt-core, dbt-postgres and dbt-duckdb next to dlt and dagster. (8) CI passes with 100% line and branch coverage on the adops package, and the only `pragma: no cover` is for TYPE_CHECKING. The Docker E2E job proves these scenarios: Sync, then Transform, then dbt tests pass; an injected Breaking Change halts the Sync Step and the Transform Step after it; a failing user-declared Check and a failing dbt test each stop later Steps; accept-schema recovers the run; the DuckDB Warehouse run passes.

confirmed: 'Halting the Step and everything after it' means Steps keep their linear YAML order. There is no explicit `needs:` graph this horizon, so 'downstream' means 'every later Step in the Pipeline'.

Breaking Change detection compares the Source table's live shape (measured before copying, alongside the existing SourceFacts pre-load Checks) with the stored snapshot. A pure domain rule classifies the difference: renamed or dropped column, or changed type, is a Breaking Change; an added column is not. A rename is detected as a drop plus an add, and is reported as a Breaking Change.
A Breaking Change only ever comes from a Source table during a Sync Step, as the GLOSSARY defines it. Shape changes in dbt models are not checked for Breaking Changes.

An 'empty Source table' error is raised before loading, from the measured Source row count. It is a dedicated error, not a failed min_rows Check. If a user also declares min_rows, that Check still decides on its own.
freshness is measured as the newest value of a column the user names, compared with a max age. The domain rule takes 'now' as an input (clock port), so it stays deterministic and testable.
User-declared Checks on a Sync table run after the load, against the Warehouse copy. They extend the horizon-1 LoadFacts and evaluate_*_checks rules rather than adding a second Check mechanism.
The demo dbt project ships a hand-written sources.yml that points at dlt's normalized raw_<source> schema and tables. adops does not generate sources.yml this horizon.
The dbt profile is generated from adops.yaml, or read through dbt env_var() from Secret References, so no password is written to disk in the Project or the tool repo (ADR-0007).
The orchestrator keeps its horizon-1 shape: in-process Dagster, Steps run in order, secrets passed only by closure, and the Transform Step added as another op behind the existing orchestrator port.
The DuckDB Warehouse is a file-based Warehouse selected per Environment in adops.yaml. Its E2E can run in the same CI job without a new Docker service.

100% branch coverage of the dbtRunner adapter. dbtRunner, run_results.json parsing and the dbt profile writing need fakes and fixture run_results files. A real dbt run only happens in E2E, so adapter branches (dbt crash compared with a test failure, a missing run_results.json) must be covered by unit tests without gaming them with pragmas.

Secret leaks through dbt. dbt logs, run_results.json messages, compiled SQL and exception text can echo connection strings or profile values. Every dbt output that adops surfaces must be sanitized, and tests must assert this (ADR-0007, the vision's secret-safety invariant).

Pure-verdict invariant (decisions.md). dbt decides its own test status. Turning dbt tests into Checks must reduce dbt's output to measured facts (failure count per test) and re-decide the verdict in a domain rule, or the binding 'adapters only measure' decision is broken.

DuckDB single-writer lock (ADR-0004). dlt's load and dbt-duckdb writing to the same DuckDB file in one in-process run can deadlock or fail with 'database is locked' if connections are not closed between Steps.

DuckDB parity. dlt's duckdb destination may map types and normalize identifiers differently from Postgres, which can break sources.yml and model SQL. The same snapshot types can also differ by Warehouse. 'Same Pipelines run unchanged' may need Warehouse-specific type normalization in the snapshot rule.

Breaking Change false positives. Postgres type aliases (varchar compared with character varying, int4 compared with integer), column order and dlt's added _dlt_* columns can all trigger spurious Breaking Changes unless the snapshot records Source-side shape in a normalized form.

Snapshot write atomicity. Recording the snapshot only after a successful run means a run that crashes after loading but before writing the snapshot leaves the snapshot out of date. Writing it per table, compared with once per run, must be decided so that a partial run cannot silently accept a Breaking Change.

Horizon-1 discovery: InOrderOrchestrator catches only StepError. New Check rules, dbtRunner exceptions or snapshot-table errors that raise anything else escape run_pipeline, so every new failure must be mapped to a StepError subtype.

phases.name: Add Breaking Change rule and halt Sync Step
phases.goal: Give the domain a pure rule that compares a Source table's current shape (column names and normalized types) with its last recorded schema snapshot and lists every Breaking Change: a dropped column, a renamed column (seen as a drop plus an add) or a retyped column. An added column is not a Breaking Change. Then make a Sync Step use that rule: make a Sync Step compare each table's preflight shape with its stored schema snapshot through a new SchemaSnapshotStore port. On any Breaking Change, the whole Step fails before any table loads and every later Step is skipped. The current shapes are saved as the new snapshot only after all of the Step's Checks pass. A first run with no snapshot records a baseline.
phases.rationale: adops needs one pure rule that decides what a Breaking Change is (dropped, renamed or retyped column; an added column is fine), and a Sync Step that applies it before any data is copied. This is one small slice across the domain and application layers: the rule has no other consumer, so it ships with the Step change that uses it. Saving the snapshot only after every Check passes means a failed run can never quietly accept a changed shape.
changes: Create src/adops/domain/schema_snapshot.py with a frozen TableShape (an immutable mapping of column name to normalized type) and a frozen BreakingChange value (column, kind dropped|retyped, previous type, current type, and a plain message that holds no row values).

Add normalize_column_type(raw: str) -> str: lowercase it, collapse whitespace, and map Postgres aliases to one canonical spelling (character varying -> varchar, int4 -> integer, int8 -> bigint, timestamp with time zone -> timestamptz, bool -> boolean, and so on).
